title: Decide whether an allOf deferral may mask a later fail (registry conflict)
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/combinators.ts:19 `results.find((r) => r.status !== 'pass') ?? results[0]`
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/resolveStepAcceptance.ts:28-29 overlay replaces ANY local deferred with a server pass/fail
registry: game-production acceptance-verdict-spine/techniques/first-non-pass-reporting-in-all-of.md Decision rules: "When a member is not-measured and a later one fails, the not-measured member still speaks"
probe: 192 allOf steps x seeded entities, mutation {one unresolved link, wiringContract.grantedBy:'TBD'} -> 283 entity-steps / 12 steps report deferred instead of fail
body:
## Summary
`allOf` reports the first non-pass, so a `deferred` member (unresolved link, runtime gate) speaks over a later member that FAILS. In this repo deferred is config-complete and `serverVerdictOverlay` can turn it into a drain pass, so the hidden fail can read green.

## Description
combinators.ts:19 returns the first non-pass. The registry technique first-non-pass-reporting-in-all-of explicitly keeps that rule ("the not-measured member still speaks") and rejects worst-severity ordering. What the technique does not model is this repo's overlay: resolveStepAcceptance.ts:28-29 lets a persisted server pass/fail replace ANY local deferred. The deferral may have come from an L2 link member while the drain ran the step's L3 test. Then a wiring-contract fail hidden behind the deferral is replaced by pass. docs/catalog/WIRING-AND-ACCEPTANCE.md:73 already tells authors to put `selected(...)` LAST so a deferral does not mask a fail, i.e. ordering is the only defence. A fix was built and reverted in this round (c2a23e47 / 60bc8074): shared `spokeIndex` = first fail/pending, else first deferred, used by allOf and explainAcceptance. Two alternatives keep the standard: (a) make `serverVerdictOverlay` refuse to lift a local deferred whose allOf has a later fail; (b) a spec-linter rule that a deferred-capable member (linksResolve, graphNodesResolve, *Deferred) may not precede a fail-capable member.

## Flow
- author composes allOf(minCount, linksResolve(), wiringContractSound()) (achievements.ts:266)
- entity links an unseeded target -> linksResolve deferred; wiring stub -> fail
- step reports deferred (config-complete); drain may overlay pass
- operator decides: change allOf (contradicts the registry technique, then file the lead), or apply (a)/(b) to keep it

## Expected impact
Catalog operators stop seeing config-complete steps that carry a failing wiring contract. Changing allOf could flip unproduced steps that compose a deferred member first from deferred to pending.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failing member is never hidden behind a deferral
Before: 283 masked entity-steps (12 distinct steps) under one realistic mutation; 0 with clean stub data
After: 0 / 0 with the reverted spokeIndex change; produce-accept + 18 acceptance test files green
Method: probe - probe test over every registered allOf step x seeded entity, with and without the mutation
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: Cache the UE header corpus once per sweep in cppSymbolExists
instrument: timing wrapper around verifyStaticAll({}, defaultStaticVerifyDeps, {apply:false}) on the real tree, plus a readFileSync call counter
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/ueStaticCheckers.ts:357-360 filesContain walks Source/ and reads every .h on EVERY call
UE tree: 292 .h files, 1.7 MB; probe: 20.6 ms per miss call (node, 20 iterations)
69 cppSymbolExists + 22 seedRowPresent declarations across pipelines; 806 pipeline_artifacts rows
body:
## Summary
Each `cppSymbolExists` call re-walks `Source/` and re-reads all 292 headers, so a static sweep reads the header tree once per check per artifact.

## Description
ueStaticCheckers.ts:357-368: `filesContain` -> `walk` -> `readFileSync` on every header, per call, no reuse. verifyStaticAll (staticVerify.ts:204) runs every declared check for every persisted row, and the settle route runs it again. Fix: a corpus read once per sweep (keyed by root, scoped to one verifyStaticAll / packaging run, not a module-level cache that goes stale) and the checkers test against the joined text.

## Flow
- measure: time verifyStaticAll dry-run on the real tree, count reads
- build a per-sweep header corpus passed through deps
- re-measure on the same filter

## Expected impact
verify-static and settle get faster and read 292 files once instead of 292 x N. Risk: a stale corpus if it outlives a sweep.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - sweep cost scales with headers, not headers x checks
Before: 20.6 ms and 292 file reads per check call (probe)
After: not measured - sweep-level timing needs the real deps wired, which this round did not build
Method: probe - per-call timing only; the sweep-level rung needs the instrument
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Extract one selected-candidate grader shared by gallery and bespoke items
instrument: existing galleryGrading + items-bespoke tests pinned before/after; LOC count of the two bodies
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:203-245 gradeGeneratedAsset
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/galleryArtifact.ts:141-203 gradeGallerySelection
header of gradeGeneratedAsset: "Same rules, same tiers and the same wording" - ~40 duplicated lines incl. three identical reason strings
body:
## Summary
`gradeGeneratedAsset` copies `gradeGallerySelection`'s no-history / unresolved / swatch branches and wording verbatim, so one rule lives in two places.

## Description
The two differ only in the leading index check (and the index-projection check, which the bespoke steps cannot have). The rest (no history -> deferred L4, unresolved selection -> fail L1, real asset -> pass L1, swatch -> deferred L4) is duplicated text. Extract `gradeSelectedCandidate(data, label)` in galleryArtifact.ts and have both call it. This round already had to edit one copy (the integer-index fix) and not the other.

## Flow
- extract the shared tail
- gradeGallerySelection = index check + projection check + shared tail
- gradeGeneratedAsset = shared tail

## Expected impact
One edit point for the gallery honesty rules. Could break: a reason string a test pins, if it is reworded.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the selected-candidate rule
Before: 2 copies, ~40 duplicated lines
After: 1 copy (walked: the 4 branches map 1:1, tests pin behaviour not location)
Method: simulation - walked the 4 branches; not built to keep the round Lane-A only
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Move genHistory out of components so acceptance lib stops importing UI tree
instrument: grep count of src/lib/** imports from @/components/**
body:
## Summary
Four server-side acceptance modules import the gallery history model from `@/components/layout-lab/...`, so the grading spine depends on the UI tree.

## Description
genHistory.ts is a pure data model but lives under components/layout-lab (sibling context catalog-browser-ui). galleryArtifact.ts also imports genericGalleryCandidates from there. Server routes (verify-static, settle, bind-icons) therefore transitively load component-tree modules. Fix: move the pure model to src/lib/catalog/genHistory.ts and re-export from the old path. That is out of scope here (sibling-owned file).

## Flow
- move genHistory + genericGalleryCandidates pure parts to lib
- leave a re-export at the old path
- count lib->components imports before/after

## Expected impact
Server grading no longer reaches into the UI folder; layout-lab refactors cannot break the grader. Risk: import cycles during the move.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - acceptance lib has no components dependency
Before: 4 acceptance files import @/components/**
After: 0 (by construction of the move)
Method: probe - grep of the import lines
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Restrict packaged file references to project roots and validate package dir ids
instrument: scan of stored packaging manifests counting referenced paths outside generated/ and the UE root; unit test with an outside path
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/packaging/collect.ts:91 looksLikeFile accepts any absolute path (drive letter or leading /) with a packageable extension
src/lib/catalog/packaging/packageArtifacts.ts:103-112 reads + hashes it and counts it as staged
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/packagingGrade.ts:47-52 any staged file -> L2 pass
src/lib/catalog/packaging/packageArtifacts.ts:85 pkgDir = `${packagesRoot}/${catalogId}/${entityId}` with unvalidated ids
body:
## Summary
A sibling artifact (LLM-produced data) can name any absolute file on the machine; the packager reads and hashes it and the packaging step grades L2 pass on it.

## Description
collect.ts:91 treats any absolute path with a known extension as a package input. packageArtifacts.ts:103 reads it, and packagingGrade.ts:47 passes on staged > 0. A step can pass on C:/Windows/.../x.png, which has nothing to do with the entity. The package dir is also built from raw catalogId/entityId (packageArtifacts.ts:85), so an id containing `..` writes manifest.json outside packagesRoot. Fix: allow only paths under the repo generated/ dirs and the bound UE root (realpath re-check, like the asset routes), and slug-check the ids.

## Flow
- artifact data names an absolute file outside the project
- verify-packaging stages + hashes it
- packaging step stores pass
- fix: allow-list roots, report others as missing with a reason

## Expected impact
Packaging pass means files of this project. Could break: stored packages that legitimately reference an absolute UE path outside the bound root.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a package cannot pass on an unrelated file
Before: any absolute path accepted (walked: 3 cases - generated/, UE Content, C:/Windows - all staged)
After: only the first two staged (predicted)
Method: simulation - live manifest scan not run this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Replace the hardcoded per-user UE root fallback with the game binding
instrument: unit test of resolveUeRoot with POF_UE_ROOT unset on a tree without the literal path
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/ueStaticCheckers.ts:337 `const fallback = 'C:\\Users\\kazda\\Documents\\Unreal Projects\\PoF'`
src/lib/games/ueBinding.ts already resolves per-game roots (ueRootForGame)
body:
## Summary
`resolveUeRoot` falls back to a literal path under one user's Documents folder; on any other machine every L2 static check silently defers as "UE root not found".

## Description
ueStaticCheckers.ts:337 hardcodes the developer path. games/ueBinding.ts already owns engine-root binding for non-PoF games, with an unbound reason. PoF should resolve through the same binding (env or declared engine.root) and report the unbound reason, not a literal per-user path.

## Flow
- POF_UE_ROOT unset on a second machine
- resolveUeRoot -> null
- every static check defers; settlePlan cause says set POF_UE_ROOT
- fix: resolve PoF via ueRootForGame(DEFAULT_GAME)

## Expected impact
Portable static verification; the unbound reason names the config. Could break: the owner machine if the binding is not declared.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no per-user literal in the grading path
Before: 1 hardcoded user path
After: 0 (walked: owner machine with env, owner without env, other machine)
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Stop one unreadable file aborting the whole static and packaging sweep
instrument: test with a dangling symlink / EACCES file under a temp Source/ (symlink creation needs privilege on Windows, hence not built here)
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/ueStaticCheckers.ts:351 fs.statSync(p) and :359 readFileSync with no try
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/staticVerify.ts:95,104 checks.map((c) => c(root)) outside safeAccept - a throw escapes verifyStaticAll and fails the route
body:
## Summary
Static checkers run outside `safeAccept`; a dangling symlink or locked file under `Source/` throws from `walk` and aborts the whole sweep instead of degrading that one check.

## Description
gradeArtifact wraps checkers in safeAccept, but staticVerify calls UeCheckers directly. walk() statSyncs every entry with no guard, so one broken link (common in UE trees with Intermediate junctions) throws out of verifyStaticAll, and settle, which chains it. Fix: skip unreadable entries in walk/filesContain and report them, or wrap each UeChecker so a throw becomes a deferred row with the error as reason.

## Flow
- a broken junction exists under Source/
- verify-static walks it
- statSync throws ENOENT
- route 500s, no row graded

## Expected impact
One bad file costs one check, not the sweep. Could break: nothing graded today changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a sweep survives an unreadable file
Before: 1 throw aborts all rows (walked)
After: only the affected check defers (walked)
Method: simulation - instrument needs a privileged symlink
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Replace raw NUL bytes in seven more source files with an escape
instrument: noRawControlBytes.test.ts widened from acceptance/packaging to src/
evidence: node scan of src/**/*.ts(x) for byte 0x00: src/app/api/judge-verdicts/route.ts, src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/changes/route.ts, src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/useGeneratedImageAssets.ts, src/lib/audio-gen/prompt-hash.ts, src/lib/craft/craft-verdicts-db.ts, src/lib/judge/fleetPlan.ts, src/__tests__/lib/judge/calibration.test.ts
body:
## Summary
Seven files outside this context hold a literal NUL byte (a key separator), so git shows every change to them as "Bin N -> M bytes".

## Description
Fixed for pythonDrain.ts this round (547bcc52) with a guard over acceptance/ and packaging/. The same pattern sits in 7 files owned by other contexts. Replace each raw byte with the \u0000 escape (same runtime string) and widen the guard to src/.

## Flow
- scan src for 0x00
- rewrite each as the \u0000 escape
- widen noRawControlBytes.test.ts ROOTS to src

## Expected impact
Every diff of those files becomes reviewable text. Nothing at runtime changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - all sources are text to git
Before: 7 files with a raw NUL
After: 0 (as measured on pythonDrain.ts: same string, test green)
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Decide whether a python bridge error should stop the entity chain
instrument: pythonDrain.test.ts case: step1 run -> {ok:false}, assert step2 not dispatched
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/pythonDrain.ts:240-245 bridge-error -> errors++ ; continue (broken stays false)
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/pythonDrain.ts:118-120 header: a chain stops after a step the re-grade condemns
body:
## Summary
When a step's module cannot be reached, the drain still dispatches the downstream steps of that entity, which then fail as consequences of a step that never ran.

## Description
The header argues that consequence failures are noise and stops the chain on a condemned step. A bridge error is the stronger case: the upstream step definitely did not run, yet the bridge-error branch continues without setting `broken`. Under an editor that dies mid-run, every later step is dispatched against missing inputs.

## Flow
- import_clips -> bridge error (editor closed)
- retarget dispatched anyway
- retarget fails: input clips missing
- recorded as an independent fail

## Expected impact
Fewer consequence-fail rows after an editor crash. Could break: an operator who relies on later steps running independently.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - consequences are not recorded as findings
Before: chain continues after bridge error (walked 3-step chain: 2 consequence fails)
After: 0 consequence fails, 2 upstream-failed skips
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
